Chris Kimm, with Equinix, spoke to the importance of the data center industry. he addressed concerns he has with some concepts put forth for Phase 1 and Phase 2 of Data Center Uses and Standards. He spoke in support of a grandfathering resolution.
James Russell spoke about community security in the US
Colleen David spoke in opposition to the grandfathering resolution of data centers currently in process. She cited general concerns with the data center industry.
Thomas David outlined his many concerns with the data center industry in Loudoun County.
Maria Saab spoke in support of the data center industry and support of a grandfathering resolution.
Scott Pedowitz with the apartment and office building association spoke in support of the grandfathering resolution of data centers.
Roger Smith spoke in support of the data centers and was not in favor of a grandfathering resolution.
Gem Bingol read Mary Terpak's comments into the record as she could not be present. She spoke in opposition of the grandfathering resolution.
Mario Zampiello VP of business development of William A Hazel. He spoke in support of the data center industry.
Mark Pontello spoke in support of the data center industry and noted the positive job creation of the industry.
Patricia Steggerda, resident of Ashburn, spoke in opposition to the data center industry, citing the negative affect they have on home values, health and safety of residents.
Jeff Tarae, commercial real estate developer, he spoke in support of the grandfathering resolution for data centers but against the 500 ft setback requirement.
